threads.title: A candidate predictor was recorded after the moment the model will be used, or after the outcome itself
threads.detector: Timing is judged against a declared moment of use, which is settled first. Under prediction it is a new field on set_intended_use (admission, index visit, baseline exam). Under inference it is clin-time-zero's time_zero reading. Three signals then order the questions, and none of them settles one. (a) Dates, outcome-blind: a predictor's own date, or its encounter's date, falls after the moment of use, or after the diagnosis, event or censoring date, for some share of rows. (b) Names and codebook, outcome-blind: process-of-care tokens (escalation, discharge, los, post_, response, treatment, follow-up). Names only order (§14.3). Negative fixture: clinical_risk's length_of_stay_days fires the 'los' token but is legitimately known at discharge for readmit_30d, so the answer 'known at the moment of use' keeps it. (c) Under prediction only, inside the training folds and recorded as an outcome view: each candidate's single-predictor AUC or R², its drop-column share of the full model's discrimination, and the label agreement of a one-threshold rule. The scan flags a single AUC ≥ 0.90, agreement ≥ 0.98, or one column carrying ≥ 90% of importance. Value test: the scan must reject a genuinely strong pre-outcome marker. clinical_risk's best single AUC is 0.645 (prior_admissions_12mo). The scan cannot be the only net. On leaky_sepsis, abx_escalation_score has AUC 1.000 and agrees with sepsis on 160/160 rows, but los_days has AUC 0.505 and is just as unavailable at admission. Under inference there is no scan and no new question, because the existing after_exposure question covers every covariate.
threads.meaning: For each flagged column, when it is known relative to the moment of use: before, at, after, or derived from the outcome. This is a new ledger kind, predictor_timing. It is asked only of flagged columns, one at a time, in order of consequence (§14.2). A 'derived from the outcome' answer hands the column to clin-outcome-defined-by-predictors. The score never settles it.

threads.title: The outcome is defined from columns in the table, as a threshold of a measurement or a composite of components
threads.detector: The outcome-blind step comes first. It pairs the outcome with candidate columns by name, label and codebook (OUTCOME_MEASURE guesses; 'diabetes' beside hba1c, glucose or a glucose-lowering drug; metabolic syndrome beside waist, TG, HDL, BP and glucose) and checks them against a table of standard cut-points (HbA1c 6.5%, FPG 126 mg/dL, BP 130/80 or 140/90). Pairing only orders the question. Under prediction, inside the training folds and recorded as an outcome view, an exact-reconstruction search runs over the codebook-paired columns and the standard cut table only, not as a combinatorial dredge. For a binary outcome it looks for a rule of at most 3 thresholds (AND/OR) whose sensitivity and specificity are both ≥ 0.99. Raw agreement is not used, because an all-zeros rule scores 98% at 2% prevalence. For a continuous outcome it looks for a sum with R² ≥ 0.999. Value test: strong non-definitional predictors fall well short. Occasion test: a defining analyte measured on an earlier occasion than the outcome (baseline HbA1c for incident diabetes) is a prognostic predictor, not incorporation, and is not flagged. Under inference the question comes from the codebook, and the search runs only after the lock, as a diagnostic. The search outputs only the definitional verdict and the cut-points, never an association.

threads.detector: clinical.read_unit_split and mixed_units_finding look for two value populations whose mode ratio matches a known conversion factor within tolerance (glucose 18.0, creatinine 88.4). The factor table widens to cholesterol 38.67, triglycerides 88.57, 25(OH)D 2.496 (ng/mL → nmol/L), hemoglobin 10 (g/dL → g/L) and vitamin D intake 40 (µg → IU). A biological subgroup spreads across sites and matches no factor. clinical_labs, re-measured: 102 values with median 6.1 and 186 with median 116.5 (ratio 19.1). threads.title: A trajectory no body follows: an adult grows 9 cm, loses a third of body weight in three weeks, or has a record dated after death
threads.detector: clinical.read_temporal and temporal_implausibility_finding compare within-person change between consecutive dated visits against physiological rates: adult height changing by more than 5 cm, weight swinging beyond a set fraction within a window, measurements dated after death. Impossible cells are removed first, so only individually believable values are judged. With three or more visits, the detector names the odd visit by the majority of the trajectory. It also shows the values implied by other columns at the same visit (BMI from height and weight) as a second witness, because the majority can be a carried-forward error. A down-then-up pattern (182 → 158 → 181 cm) points to two people under one ID. clinical_labs: PT0007's height runs 167.6 → 176.6 → 176.6 cm, a transposed first entry. PT0021's weight runs 67.9 → 44.7 → 45.7 kg at a constant 179.8 cm, so the later two agree and the first visit (or a second person) is the odd one; but 45 kg at 179.8 cm is a BMI near 14. longitudinal_visits: P000 goes 97.8 → 66.6 kg in a month.

threads.title: One reading or one blood draw is a noisy measure of a person's usual level (regression dilution)
threads.detector: Outcome-blind, from three sources in order of what they can show. Between-visit repeat draws in a subsample give the ICC (λ) for the usual level, and these are the practical trigger. An external within-person CV from a biological-variation table (CRP high, triglycerides moderate, cholesterol low) is used only when disclosed as an assumption. Within-visit replicate columns (BPXSY1-4; bp_1-bp_3) give the within-person SD and the first-reading offset (the alerting reaction). Their λ is an upper bound that will rarely fall below 0.8. top_moments: 1. A leak the score rewards (clin-predictor-after-prediction-time, measured on leaky_sepsis). 'abx_escalation_score agrees with sepsis on all 160 admissions. When was it recorded?' One tap, 'after sepsis was suspected', and the score settles from 1.00 to 0.81. Then: 'los_days doesn't separate at all (AUC 0.51), but it is also known only at discharge.' A pipeline that optimizes the score keeps the first column and never asks about the second.

2. Two labs, not two kinds of patients (clin-mixed-units with clin-site-differences, measured on clinical_labs). All 102 low glucose values (median 6.1) are SOUTH; NORTH's 186 have median 116.5. The predictors tell the sites apart perfectly (C = 1.00), and all of it is glucose's unit; without glucose, C = 0.53. Unconverted, the model learns 'low glucose, fewer readmissions', which is really a site difference.

3. Rows are visits, not people (clin-encounters-not-patients, structure measured on clinical_labs). '288 rows are 96 patients seen three times. Split by row, two of each patient's visits train the model that is scored on the third.' The score gap still needs a fixture with a patient-level signal.

4. The drug's reading, not the patient's (clin-treated-measurements, measured on NHANES). 'People on BP medication have the same SBP as diagnosed people who aren't treated (135.1 vs 135.3).' The transform player adds Tobin's constant and the treated hump moves right. The NHANES file is untracked, so a derived fixture must be committed.

5. The model would be reading the definition (clin-outcome-defined-by-predictors with clin-diagnosed-not-diseased; needs a fixture). The app shows the rule it found: 'diabetes = 1 exactly when hba1c ≥ 6.5 or glucose ≥ 126'. It then asks: 'Do you want to predict having diabetes, or being diagnosed with it?' About a third of US diabetes is undiagnosed (Menke 2015).

6. No follow-up means no forecast (clin-diagnostic-or-prognostic, from the existing follow-up answer). 'There is no follow-up here, so this model finds people who already have diabetes. Some of its best predictors (low sugar intake, metformin) are consequences of being diagnosed.' The paper's verb changes from 'predicts' to 'identifies'.

7. Your lowest values aren't missing (clin-censored-lab-results, measured on clinical_labs). 'One patient in five has a CRP below 0.3. Those aren't missing: they're your lowest values.' 55 of 288 rows; dropped, the median moves up. Above the pack's share, the handling becomes an asked slot instead of a silent substitution.

8. A state, not an event (clin-state-or-event, measured on clinical_longitudinal). 'Progression rises from 20% to 33% by visit, yet 67 of 200 people un-progressed. Is progression something a patient can recover from?' The answer chooses between survival, GEE or multi-state, and recurrent-event models.

9. Protection manufactured by the clock (clin-time-zero; needs a fixture). Each person's timeline is drawn with the 'immortal' segment before exposure lit. Users had to survive 2 years to count as users. Re-anchored at time zero after the lock, the advantage shrinks.
10. Sick, not erroneous (clin-impossible-vs-extreme, measured on clinical_labs). 'These 4 are impossible; these 26 are sick. A generic outlier rule would have removed all 30.'

## Clinical catalog: final version, 54 threads

I applied the critic's verdicts and returned the catalog. I made no changes to the repo.

### What changed
- **Cuts:** none. Neither the AutoML skeptic nor the evidence checker rejected any of the 50 threads.
- **Fixes:** all 31 were applied.
- **Automate-silently threads:** all 4 moved, two to silent and two to stated:
  - clin-digit-preference → silent;
  - clin-sparse-levels-separation → silent, and moved to the shared lens because it is generic (dedupe it against the shared catalog);
  - clin-age-time-scale → stated, with attained age presented as a disputed convention (Pencina 2007);
  - clin-event-found-at-visits → stated.
- **New threads from the critic's missing list:**
  - clin-preclinical-disease-before-event;
  - clin-self-report-vs-measured;
  - clin-population-specific-cutoffs;
  - clin-specimen-quality-flags.

  The other two missing items were folded in: the wider unit-factor table (now including affine HbA1c and °F/°C) into clin-mixed-units, and lab H/L reference flags into clin-derived-clinical-variables. **The four new threads have not been through the critic, and their references are from memory.**

### Tiers (BLUEPRINT §11.4)
- 30 asked, 18 stated, 4 stated-and-surfaced, 2 silent.
- "Surfaced" is not a fourth tier. It means a stated decision whose noticing also shows on the canvas without blocking (informative test ordering, coding transition, loss to follow-up, calendar drift).
- Most asked threads only fire under a condition, and each tier string says which. Every thread carries the critic's rank signal.

### Rules applied across threads
- **Names never settle a reading (§14.3).** They only order questions. This affects:
  - the process-of-care tokens; `length_of_stay_days` in clinical_risk is now the false-positive fixture;
  - case-control labels and round outcome shares;
  - arm names; randomization is asked, and the balance C only flags a doubtful arm;
  - established-set columns; the base model is asked, pre-filled;
  - baseline-disease labels.
- **Purpose-rule leaks are closed.** These views now wait for the lock under inference:
  - the immortal-time tell;
  - per-site and per-period outcome rates;
  - the ferritin–CRP slope when ferritin is the outcome;
  - expected-direction checks, which compare the exposure's sign only.
- **RO-01 is extended through a new `outcome_definition` reading.** It generalizes the two existing refusals in `turbotab/core/structural.py`: line 442 (no predictor) and line 456 (no eligibility rule). That also governs eGFR and HbA1c exclusions.
- **Predictor timing needs a declared moment of use first.** That moment is a new field on `set_intended_use`, which has none today (`turbotab/core/decisions.py:1630`). Under inference the same moment is the `time_zero` reading.

### Evidence
- **Measured on fixtures and kept:**
  - leaky_sepsis: 160/160 agreement; CV AUC 1.00 → 0.81 without the leaking column.
  - clinical_risk: best single AUC 0.645.
  - clinical_labs (I re-checked several of these):
    - glucose splits 102/186 at ratio 19.1, all 102 low values at SOUTH;
    - PT0021's weight runs 67.9 → 44.7 → 45.7 kg at 179.8 cm;
    - PT0007's height runs 167.6 → 176.6 → 176.6 cm;
    - dbp 78 and 82 hold 3.1% each;
    - censored CRP on 19.1%;
    - 4 impossible SBPs against 26 real values above 200;
    - 96 patients × 3 visits;
    - site membership C 1.00 → 0.53 without glucose.
  - clinical_longitudinal: 67 of 200 people revert.
  - clinic_visits: now the negative fixture for single-reading dilution (ICC 0.95).
  - NHANES: SBP 135.1 vs 135.3, treated vs diagnosed-untreated.
- **Every magic line without a fixture now uses bracketed values** computed from the user's data instead of invented numbers.

### Fixture debts
Each thread needs a positive and a negative fixture before it ships (§14.3):
- **Outcome and design:** definitional outcome; diagnosed vs disease (needs HbA1c and DIQ010); fasting; cohort with prevalent cases, competing death, dropout and immortal time; matched case-control; trial with crossover and intercurrent events; partial verification.
- **Time:** a patient-level signal plus the readmission-equals-next-row leak; drift spanning 3 years or more; a coding transition; an assay step; between-visit repeats.
- **Biomarkers:** season of draw; BRINDA; pregnancy; derived eGFR or Friedewald LDL; contraindication bands; children.
- **Codes and visits:** code matrix; outcome-driven visits.
- **The four new threads.**

### Engine work, in order of consequence
1. The `outcome_definition` kind, feeding the structural.py refusals.
2. The moment of use and a `predictor_timing` kind.
3. A unit-conversion repair family (user-executed) with the site cross.
4. A `treated_by` kind and the treatment card.
5. The seal records censored-at-limit values instead of substituting.
6. The opening card's read-from-data block.
7. The shared known-date step detector.
8. One heaping detector for default values and digit preference.
9. The follow-up card additions: competing event, recurrent event and the short-follow-up count.

### Housekeeping for Nolan
- `turbotab/sample_data/clinical_labs.md` still gives the glucose split as 120/168 at 18.6; it should be 102/186 at 19.1.
- `/Users/nhedglin/tabular-ml-lab/_tt_tmp_nhanes.csv` is untracked and owner-only. Commit a derived fixture, with the `imputed_bp_*` rows excluded from the terminal-digit control.
- The critic's web lookups hit a session limit, so these references are unverified: the TRIPOD+AI item numbers (9a, 12e, 23a, 27a), STREGA 9b/11, Pencina 2007, the diet → biomarker edge citations, and all references in the four new threads.
